summary: Phase 3 Workout Player backend enhancements verified: 10/10 new tests PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_workout_player_phase3.py covering (1) cardio pace auto-derivation, (2) explicit pace preservation, (3) null pace when only duration provided, (4) warmup+timer persistence, (5) HR/calories persistence, (6) GET /workouts/{wid}/sets round-trips all cardio fields, (7) progression 'increase' (80kg×8 @ RPE 7.0 → suggested 82.5, delta +2.5, reason contains 'Hit target reps' and 'RPE 7'), (8) progression 'hold' (RPE 9 → 80.0, delta 0), (9) progression uncertain (rpe=None → hold with 'log RPE' reason), and (10) weighted-set regression (existing fields still persist correctly; new cardio fields default to null). Regression on /api/coach/exercises/{name:path}/generate-image: 7/7 tests pass, but with intermittent Cloudflare 502s at the ingress during bursty full-suite runs — every individual retry passes cleanly. This exactly matches iteration_21's documented behavior; no code change needed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1617 — auto pace derivation guarded by 'not doc.get(pace_sec_per_km) and duration_sec and distance_m'. Confirmed explicit pace is preserved and null-only-duration keeps pace null. Correct.

server.py:1663 — hit_reps compares actual_reps to the LOWER bound of a target_reps range like '8-10' via split('-')[0]. That is the correct progressive-overload semantics (hit at least the min prescribed).
server.py:1666 — suggested = round(wt + max(2.5, wt*0.025), 1). For 80kg → max(2.5, 2.0)=2.5 → 82.5. For 120kg → max(2.5, 3.0)=3.0 → 123.0. Rule matches spec.

server.py:1662 — top_set is the max by actual_weight; ties broken by dict order (fine for identical-weight sets). RPE taken from top_set only — if user logs 80kg×8 @ RPE7 then 80kg×8 @ RPE9 in the same session, top_set's rpe is whichever comes first in max(). Consider evaluating RPE across all sets if this matters (currently not, since target_reps hit-check IS across all sets).

server.py:1663 — small nit: str(r.get('target_reps') or 0).split('-')[0] passes through '0' when target_reps is None, and int('0')==0 so any actual_reps satisfies. That's benign but means a set with no target_reps never blocks progression.

success_rate.backend: 100% (10/10 Phase 3 + 7/7 Nano Banana regression on individual runs)

seed_data_creation: Each test uses a unique exercise_name suffixed with uuid4().hex[:6] and prefixed 'TEST_' (e.g. TEST_Cardio_Auto_a1b2c3, TEST_Prog_Increase_...). These write to db.workout_sets under the client user for the first seeded workout id from /workouts/week. Data is scoped per-exercise-name so it does NOT pollute progression logic for real exercises. No cleanup performed (safe — clearly namespaced).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 3 endpoints (cardio + progression + warmup) are stable. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_workout_player_phase3.py for regression. If Cloudflare 502s appear on Nano Banana suite during bursty runs, retry individually — iteration_21 and iteration_22 both confirm this is infra flake, not a code bug. When testing progression logic, always use unique exercise names per test to avoid last_session bleed-over (helper _log_two_sets already does this).
rca_of_issue: N/A — all Phase 3 tests pass on first try; Nano Banana suite failures are ingress-layer Cloudflare 502s (HTML response body confirms Cloudflare origin), transient under concurrent load. Individual retries always succeed. Same signature as iteration_21.
